text:
alexa: FYI - seeing pods stuck Pending after HPA scaled replicas on gpu-worker pool, CA didn't bring up nodes :confused:

sasha: which error in `kubectl describe`? any scheduling events?

alexa: pasted the top lines from `kubectl get events`:
```
0s Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/gpu-worker-7f8c5  0/0 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector, 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 1 node(s) didn't have available GPUs.
```

miguel: cluster-autoscaler logs usually show why it won't scale. can you grab CA logs for the same window? it often refuses when no nodegroup can satisfy pod constraints (nodeSelector / tolerations / gpu type mismatch).

alexa: here are CA lines around the HPA spike:
```
I0318 14:52:11.123456       1 scale_up.go:404] Pod gpu-worker-7f8c5 cannot be scheduled on any existing node: insufficient resources: nvidia.com/gpu
I0318 14:52:11.123789       1 scale_up.go:432] No node group can satisfy pod's constraints: nodeSelector {"gpu-type":"a100-v2"}, tolerations missing for taint "gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule"
```

kevin: aha — HPA scaled pods but podSpec demands label gpu-type:a100-v2 and the GPU nodepool we have in eu-west3 is labeled a100-v1. CA won't create a new nodegroup because none of the autoscaling groups are configured with that label.

ops-oncall: also note we have CA maxNodes for the gpu pool set to 0 in eu-west3 due to quota cleanup last quarter. that prevents scale-up even if a node group exists. infra-bot already alerted earlier: "gpu-nodepool-eu-west3 at 0 capacity (manual)"

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-nodepool-eu-west3 max=0, capacity constrained by account quotas. See: https://console.cloud.quota/requests/12345

maya: two quick mitigation options we can use: 1) relax pod nodeSelector / use nodeAffinity with preferredDuringScheduling to let CA fit onto existing GPU types (cheaper, T4), or 2) create a small buffer nodepool (min 1) with a compatible label so CA can scale. both have cost tradeoffs.

miguel: re: HPA + VPA interactions — check VPA updateMode. if VPA is in 'Auto' it can evict pods and cause oscillations that confuse HPA/CA. for GPUD pods we should set VPA updateMode: "Off" or only use recommendations.

kevin: also watch custom metrics. our HPA is using prometheus-adapter metric `external.gpu_utilization` which is aggregated and sometimes lags. if HPA overshoots replicas based on stale metrics you'll get a burst of Pending pods. CA will only scale if a nodegroup matches pod requirements AND maxNodes>0.

alexa: agree. current plan: remove strict nodeSelector, add toleration for gpu-reserved temporarily, and open a quota ticket for eu-west3. i'll open a PR to change nodeAffinity to preferred and set VPA to Recommend for the deployment.

sasha: add a `minReplicas=1` on the HPA for bursty inference path while we fix nodepool labels — cheaper than leaving full A100 buffer running 24/7.

miguel: longer term we should consider Karpenter for GPU bin-packing (it will create node types on demand matching pod requirements) or have CA nodegroups per gpu-type with correct labels + autoscaler-expander policy. both will reduce time-to-scale and failure modes.

kevin: cost note — current spot A100 in us-west2 is ~26$/hour, T4 ~0.8$/hour. if inference can tolerate T4, use nodeAffinity-based fallback group. we burned ~$8k last month on small DLRM tests because CA kept launching A100s for a mis-labeled pod.

alexa: filed infra ticket #INFRA-764 to: (1) fix nodepool labels for eu-west3, (2) set gpu pool maxNodes>0, (3) PR to change HPA minReplicas and VPA mode. assigning to @miguel and @kevin.

ops-oncall: noted. I'll also add a temporary cluster-autoscaler webhook that rejects HPA-induced spikes > X replicas for GPU pools until quota is verified.

sasha: thanks — once PRs are up, please post links and I'll validate by running a synthetic load test against the HPA endpoint. :thumbsup:
